newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest '97 runoff seen 109 pct of normal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest '97 runoff seen 109 pct of normal.

text.p: Runoff at The Dalles dam on the Columbia River will be 109 percent of average levels for January through July next year, according to the annual "early bird" forecast from the Northwest River Forecast Center.
The Portland, Ore.-based agency sees runoff totaling 115 million acre feet, compared with 139.3 million (or 132 percent of normal) in January-July of this year.
The Dalles is the second-to-last hydroelectric project on the Columbia River.
The first official 1997 runoff forecast will be issued in early January, and the center will update its forecast each month.
Regional reservoir levels, meanwhile, are "exactly where we need them to be," according to an official with the Northwest Power Pool Coordinating Group.
"We are running right along our winter draft curve," he said.
The official noted most of the region's winter precipitation has been in the form of snow, spelling a healthy outlook for next spring's runoff.
